system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation (one-line reason) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price (A$4.8m)**. | A materially higher cap, calibrated to diligence and risk; preserve separate treatment for fundamental, tax, specific indemnity and fraud claims. | **Reject as drafted; seek a higher general cap and keep distinct caps for other claim categories**, because the proposed cap may inadequately cover identified and unknown exposure. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | A$25,000 de minimis per claim and A$250,000 tipping/deductible basket; only excess over basket recoverable. | Lower de minimis, a smaller tipping basket (or a tipping basket once crossed), and exclusions for specified indemnities and fundamental claims. | **Counter with a lower de minimis and smaller tipping basket, with carve-outs**, because the current thresholds could leave substantial valid losses unrecoverable. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | 18 months after Completion; Seller also proposes applying any general claim limitation to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | A longer general warranty period and express, category-specific periods; no blanket extension of the general period to other claims. | **Seek at least 24 months and expressly preserve longer statutory/contractual periods for tax, title, fraud and indemnity claims**, because 18 months may be too short to discover and quantify latent issues. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limits. | Separate, substantially higher cap (potentially price/consideration) and longer period for fundamental and title claims. | **Reject parity with general warranties; negotiate a separate regime**, because ownership and authority are central to the transaction. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions said to apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out stated. | Expressly exclude fraud (including fraudulent misrepresentation/concealment) from caps, thresholds, time bars, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to the extent legally permissible. | **Require an express fraud carve-out**, because the draft’s broad limitations could otherwise purport to restrict remedies for deliberate wrongdoing. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire indexed data room, Accounts, registers and public records, plus specific disclosures. | Specific, fair disclosure against the relevant warranty, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no blanket data-room or public-register disclosure. | **Reject general disclosure and require specific, warranty-linked disclosure**, because the letter itself identifies material uncertainties and broad disclosure would make warranties difficult to rely on. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | No imputed or constructive knowledge bar; at most, narrowly defined actual knowledge of named decision-makers after appropriate inquiry, with fraud and specific indemnity carve-outs. | **Reject the current qualifier**, because “discoverable” knowledge would make diligence materials a broad waiver of warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure says no final consent or evidence conditions are satisfied. | Consent and all clause 11.3 conditions satisfied before Completion as a condition precedent, with termination/extension rights and no deemed satisfaction on consent alone. | **Make fully compliant consent a condition precedent**, because Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and the disclosed conditions remain unverified. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | A release to be provided following Completion for an approximately A$3.2m facility. | Repayment at or before Completion from the funds flow, lender payout evidence and effective release of all security as completion deliverables; no residual recourse to the Company. | **Require discharge and release at Completion, not afterwards**, because the facility remains outstanding and post-Completion release leaves Buyer exposed to debt and secured claims. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | A$420,000 conditional Completion bonuses are not separately itemised in the draft funds flow; no position on payroll tax, super or on-costs. | Identify and fund the bonuses and all employer on-costs in the completion mechanics, with appropriate debt-like/leakage treatment and no double counting. | **Reconcile and deduct or fund the full accrued cost at Completion**, because the disclosed liabilities are omitted from the funds flow and may exceed A$420,000. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; Seller considers it adequate. Disclosure says transfer depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, A$180,000 remains open, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the room. | Specific indemnity covering payment, title, infringement and loss of use/remediation, plus cleared payment and executed assignment of all necessary Project Materials before Completion. | **Expand the indemnity and make payment plus assignment a Completion deliverable**, because the disclosed evidence does not establish that the Company owns or can use the materials. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | DD-006 is preliminary and not expected to be material; limitations apply to all Claims. Disclosure does not establish access, scope or notification duties. | Specific indemnity for incident-related investigation, notification, remediation, third-party and regulatory costs; ongoing cooperation and prompt disclosure, outside general cap/basket/time limits. | **Seek a separate incident indemnity and pre-Completion investigation/cooperation covenants**, because uncertainty about access and notification creates potentially uncapped regulatory and remediation exposure. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals, A$330,000 aggregate, characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Verify timing, scope, termination rights, accrual and ordinary-course status; account for unavoidable pre-Completion liabilities in price/working capital or a specific adjustment. | **Do not accept the characterisation without evidence; reconcile the commitments in completion accounts**, because the disclosure does not establish whether the renewals are avoidable or already accrued. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; Seller says tax and IP are settled under the general regime. | Expressly separate general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, fraud and other claims, with tailored caps, baskets, periods and remedies. | **Require an express claim-category schedule and precedence clause**, because applying one general regime to every claim could inadvertently constrain negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Seller as holder of 100%; no separate verification stated. | Verify issued capital, register, constitution, encumbrances and transfer mechanics; obtain title/authority warranties and duly executed transfer documents. | **Treat DD-012 as evidence, not conclusive verification, and require completion deliverables and warranties**, because the register alone does not establish absence of encumbrances or defects in transfer. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP positions settled under the general regime. | Negotiate explicit tax warranties/indemnity and IP ownership, licensing, infringement and open-source protections, with tailored survival and caps; confirm whether any terms were actually agreed. | **Mark these terms open and document them expressly**, because the Seller’s assertion of settlement is unsupported by the supplied positions and would otherwise import the inadequate general regime. |

These are buyer-side negotiation recommendations based on the supplied draft and disclosure summary; confirm against the complete SPA, diligence record and applicable Australian law.
=== END ADVICE ===
